chapter: Early career: vaudeville and Kansas City
title: Hentoff's book and the Moten-Page rhythm description
summary: Kuehl reads a description of Moten's two-beat and Page's four-beat rhythms merging in the Basie band; Basie calls it a matter of opinion.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Did you ever read Nat Hentoff's 'Ya'll?' (PHONETIC) book -- do you hear me talking to you?
No, I think -- no, I haven't.
I don't know. We'll see how accurate it is, you know?
I just saw him. (Inaudible) something to do with --

Okay, Joe says that 'Benny Moten's band played a two-beat rhythm such as one and three. Walter Page's band played a two and four. It wasn't that they would stop to accent that beat, it was sort of like a bouncing ball. Now, when those rhythms met in the Basie band, there was an
even flow -- one, two, three, four, -- like a bounding ball." Do you endorse that statement?
I don't know. That's a matter of opinion on that.
Okay, well, this is you talking now.
